chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from al-Ala', from al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked him about a man who accused his wife of adultery (li'an), he said: 'He performs li'an with her. And if he refuses to perform li'an, he is flogged with the flogging penalty, and his wife is returned to him. And if he performs li'an with her, they are separated, and she is not permissible to him until the Day of Judgment.'
And li'an is that he testifies against her: 'Four testimonies by Allah that I saw you committing adultery,' and the fifth is that he invokes a curse upon himself 'if he is of the liars.'

If she confesses, she is stoned. And if she wishes to ward off the punishment from herself, she testifies: 'Four testimonies by Allah that he is of the liars,' and the fifth is 'that the anger of Allah is upon her if he is of the truthful.'

If he disowns his child, the child is attached to his maternal uncles, they inherit him, and they do not inherit him except if he inherits his mother. And if anyone calls him 'son of adultery,' the one who calls him is flogged with the flogging penalty.'

key_terms.الْمُلاَعَنَةُ: Li'an (mutual imprecation), a specific legal procedure where a husband accuses his wife of adultery and invokes a curse upon himself if he is lying.
key_terms.رُجِمَتْ: She is stoned (to death) as punishment for adultery.
key_terms.وَلَدَ زِنًى: Son of adultery (child whose father disowned him via Li'an).

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling of Li'an and its consequences for husband and wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elaborates on the jurisprudence of Li'an, detailing the procedural steps where a husband accuses his wife of adultery without four witnesses. It specifies that if the wife refuses to undergo Li'an, she is flogged and remains married, whereas if she accepts, they are permanently separated. The text also addresses the paternity dispute, noting that the child is linked to the maternal uncles for inheritance unless the mother is involved, and clarifies the penalty for those who label the child as 'illegitimate'.
